required_facts_checked: The workflow begins with a GitHub Issue form containing a course, question and answer.
The agent loads FAQ entries and metadata and indexes section, question and answer with minsearch, using course and section_id as keyword fields.
Retrieved similar entries and course section metadata are sent with the new proposal to the model.
The structured Pydantic FAQDecision can return NEW, UPDATE or DUPLICATE.
The workflow can create a new file, update an existing entry or close a duplicate issue, and GitHub Actions opens a pull request for file changes.
The bot can misclassify sections or merge a proposal into the wrong FAQ when a match is superficially similar.
The default triage model is gpt-5-nano.
The writer reviews batches of pull requests with Claude Code, explains corrections and reviews the edited branch before merging.
Human review remains in the loop rather than allowing automatic merges.
unsupported_claims_removed: Removed claims that retrieval guarantees correct placement or that the bot can merge safely without review.
Removed unsupported performance or quality claims about the triage model.
substantive_edits: Rewrote the article as a teaching explanation of proposal intake, retrieval context, structured decisions and review.
Explained the three actions and repository effects in concrete workflow terms.
Preserved the named model, known misclassification examples and Claude Code review step.
